---
title: "Quarto"
subtitle: "Reports, slides and websites written in Markdown, with code that runs when you render"
---

## Render

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Render one document | `pixi run quarto render reports/ltee-report.qmd` |
| Render the documents listed in `_quarto.yml` | `pixi run quarto render` |
| Preview in the browser, re-rendered on every save | `pixi run quarto preview reports/first.qmd` (stop: `Ctrl-C`) |
| Change a parameter for one render | `pixi run quarto render reports/ltee-report.qmd -P max_reads:2000` |
| Another format | add `--to typst` (PDF), `--to docx` (Word) or `--to revealjs` (slides) |
| Render a Jupyter notebook, running it first | `pixi run quarto render notebooks/NOTEBOOK.ipynb --execute` |
| Render as part of the pipeline | `pixi task add report "quarto render reports/ltee-report.qmd" --depends-on download`, then `pixi run report` |

See [lesson 07, sections 3 and 6 to 9](../pages/07-quarto.qmd#your-first-quarto-document).

## The document header

```{.yaml}
---
title: "Mutations in the Long-Term Evolution Experiment"
author: "Ada Lovelace"
date: today
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true   # one self-contained HTML file
    toc: true
    code-fold: true
execute:
  warning: false
bibliography: references.bib
jupyter: python3
---
```

## Code cells and their options

````{.markdown}
```{{python}}
#| label: fig-quality
#| fig-cap: "Mean base quality along the reads."
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of mean quality against position in the read ..."
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
```
````

- `#| label: fig-NAME` or `tbl-NAME`: a numbered figure or table, cited in the text as `@fig-NAME`
- `fig-cap`, `tbl-cap`: the caption
- `fig-alt`: alt text, what the figure shows, for screen readers
- `echo: false`: hide the code, keep the output
- `include: false`: hide code and output; the cell still runs
- `eval: false`: show the code without running it
- `tags: [parameters]`: the cell whose values `-P` can change

Each option goes on its own `#|` line at the top of the cell.

## In the text

| What you want | Write |
|------------|------------------------|
| Cite a figure or table | `@fig-quality`, `@tbl-samples` |
| Cite a paper from `references.bib` | `[@tenaillon2016]` |
| Where the reference list goes | `::: {#refs}` and `:::` on the next line |
| A call-out box | `::: {.callout-note}` ... `:::` (also `-tip`, `-warning`, `-important`) |

A value computed when the report renders, never typed (inline code):

```{.markdown}
Each file has `{python} f"{n_reads:,}"` reads.
```

More Markdown on the [Markdown cheat sheet](markdown.qmd).

## `_quarto.yml` for a project

```{.yaml}
project:
  execute-dir: project   # code runs from the project folder
  render:
    - reports/*.qmd      # what a plain `quarto render` renders
```

Without it, code runs in the folder of the document, and Quarto may pick up
settings from a folder above. See [section 2](../pages/07-quarto.qmd#tell-quarto-where-the-project-is).
